title: Availability across windows
prompt: Each service promises 99% availability over the period: at least 99% of its requests without a server error. Using the 5-minute windows in `service_metrics`, write `solve` so it returns one row per service with its totals, its availability and whether it met the target.
rules: Columns and types: `service STRING, requests BIGINT, server_errors BIGINT, availability_pct DOUBLE, meets_slo BOOLEAN`.
`availability_pct` is over the whole period: `(requests - server_errors) / requests × 100`, rounded to 2 decimals, where the totals add up all the service's windows.
`meets_slo` compares the rounded value with `TARGET_PCT`; exactly 99.00 meets it.
A service whose windows have no requests at all has NULL `availability_pct`, and `meets_slo` is false.
hints: Compare catalog-api's windows in the sample: one busy and clean, one tiny and failing. What should one bad request out of a thousand weigh?
Add the counts first with `groupBy` and `F.sum`, then divide once.
Spark 4 raises an error on division by zero. `F.when(requests > 0, ...)` divides only when there's something to divide, and `otherwise(False)` makes a NULL comparison false.
explanation: Availability over a period is total good requests over total requests, so sum `request_count` and `error_count` per service and divide once. Averaging each window's percentage gives a 10-request window the same weight as a 1 000-request one: catalog-api's tiny bad window drags the average to about 75% although 99.01% of its requests worked. Round before comparing, as the rule says: search-api's 98.996% rounds to 99.00 and meets the target. A service with windows but no requests can't be divided, and with ANSI mode on the division would fail the whole query, so guard it with `F.when`, which leaves NULL; a comparison with NULL is NULL, so `meets_slo` needs `otherwise(False)`.
